items.response:
I'll send Sam an oat-milk flat white, with nothing hazelnut-flavoured, and a vegetarian snack with no fish or seafood to room 214 at Riverdale for around 3:30. He has interviews until 8 with no real break, so something filling is better than something sweet. I'll also check that the school office accepts deliveries.
Action: Find a cafe near Riverdale that can deliver by 3:30, and confirm the order with you before I place it.

I'll cover ser vs estar with emotions and locations, por vs para, and the subjunctive after cuando for future actions (cuando llegue a casa te llamo, not llego). I'll set the exercises up as short role-plays (ordering food, a work meeting, a doctor's visit) with Mexican vocabulary like carro and computadora, since that's how you learn best, and put an answer key at the end.
Action: Draft the sheet and save it to your notes before your next Thursday 8:00 pm lesson with Carlos.

Moving Leo's piano with Mrs. Greene from Mondays 4:30-5:15 to Fridays at 4:15 pm starting September 2026, which clears the clash with your Roadmap review block. I'll keep it at her place on Pape Avenue and the same 45-minute length unless you tell me otherwise, and Sam gets notifications from the shared calendar so he'll see the change.
Action: Open the shared family calendar (my notes have it under two similar names, 'Malhotra-Okafor family' and 'Okafor-Malhotra family', so I'll confirm the right one first), end the Monday series before September, add a weekly Friday 4:15 pm series from September, and check Fridays for conflicts.

On it. I'll look for an upper-intermediate Spanish grammar book that focuses on the subjunctive, with lots of exercises and a full answer key, and compare a few on content, reviews and price. I don't know your budget or whether you want Latin American Spanish specifically, so I'll flag that for each one.
Action: Send you a shortlist of 2-3 books with prices and what each covers, then order the one you pick.

I don't want to guess at what you wrote when you're about to commit to something on Monday, so I'll read your actual sent mail instead of going from memory. That way you'll have the exact wording and dates you gave Tom.
Action: Search your sent mail for messages to Tom Becker about roadmap timing and quote the exact lines back to you.

That sounds draining, standing the whole way both directions with the bag digging into your shoulder. A packed streetcar twice in one day would wear anyone out.
Action: Just listen, so go ahead and tell me more if you want to get it out.

From what I have, baking on weekend mornings with Leo is one of your favourite ways to unwind (he's good at stirring, bad at waiting). The basement kitchen only has a microwave, an induction hotplate and the old fridge, so I'd keep tomorrow no-oven and simple, something stovetop in the cast iron (the old aluminium pot won't work on the hotplate), and leave the rest of the day open.
Action: Pick one easy recipe Leo can help stir and keep tomorrow afternoon clear, and I'll set it up if you say yes.

I don't have a confirmed 2026 end date for you. My notes only have last season's pickups (the last was Tue 9 Dec 2025, paper bags only, no plastic), and the notes on your collection day don't agree with each other, so I won't guess.
Action: Look up this fall's yard waste schedule on the City of Toronto's collection calendar for your address and tell you the last pickup date; keep the leaves in paper bags meanwhile.

Got all of that, thank you, and I won't bring up the second-child topic unless you do. Biscuit's siren solo is a proud beagle tradition.
Action: Update what I have on file: Leo's birthday is July 17, 2019 (I had Oct 21, so I'll fix that and the yearly calendar entry), grade 2 at Morse Street PS with Ms. Alvarez, contact her through Edsby not email; you get Leo and Jun on Wednesdays and Hannah does Fridays; no meetings before 9:30 or after 16:30 and nothing after 15:00 on Fridays (replacing the 17:00 limit); Spanish with Carlos Méndez moves to Thursdays, homework review at 19:30 and the lesson at 8:00 pm on Zoom for 60 minutes (replacing the Tuesday 19:00 slot); and prefer Canadian retailers (MEC, Indigo, Simons) over Amazon when they ship within a week.

Adding both to Thursday's to-do list, Nate's backsplash decision and the Morse Street forms, both due Fri 30 Jan. I don't have a note of what you looked into last spring, and I don't know where Grace and Daniel live, so I can't say what's on up there in May yet.
Action: Search your notes and past chats for last spring's research, and once I know the town, look up events around the May long weekend.

Here's a draft: 'Hi team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That is 10,000 times a merchant got their money faster, and it comes from the steady work each of you put in. Thank you, in particular [name] for [specific thing] and [name] for [specific thing].' It's calm and concrete, with no exclamation marks or em dashes.
Action: Send me one or two names and what they did and I'll fill the brackets, then save the final version for you to post tomorrow.

I don't have the results from that 27 Feb VIA Rail search saved, so I can't tell you what we found, and I won't guess at times. Rerunning it is quick.
Action: Look up VIA Rail Friday evening departures from Toronto to Ottawa (times, duration, fares) for the next Friday unless you tell me a different date, and put the drive time next to it for the comparison.

Lisbon flights on TAP from Toronto Pearson, leaving Fri 18 Dec 2026 and back Wed 30 Dec 2026, going on the family calendar now. I don't have flight times, so I'll add it as a multi-day entry and fill in times if you send me the confirmation.
Action: Add 'Lisbon (TAP from Pearson), 18 Dec to 30 Dec 2026' to the 'Malhotra-Okafor family' calendar so Sam sees it.

Congratulations to you, Kabir and Mei. Ira born on Valentine's Day, February 14, 2026, in Vancouver, and you're her godmother, that's a big one.
Action: Save Ira's birthday and your godmother role to your notes, add Feb 14 as a yearly calendar entry with a reminder a week before (tell me if you'd rather not), and get back to your Spanish worksheet whenever you're ready.

Here's a draft: 'Neha, [partner's name], here's to a lifetime of one of you saying I'm fine with whatever, and the other knowing that's a trap. May you always agree on the thermostat, and when you don't, may the right one win gracefully. Congratulations, cheers.' I don't have the partner's name, so there's a placeholder.
Action: Fill in the name once you send it, and adjust the jokes if you want something more specific to the two of them.

I don't have the results of that 27 Feb search saved, so I can't say what we found. Since you normally prefer driving the Mazda to Ottawa (about 452 km, 4 h 35 min without traffic, leaving early Friday), that search was probably just a comparison.
Action: Rerun the VIA Rail Friday evening times from Toronto to Ottawa and put them next to the drive, so you can compare.

On it. I'll sort the March break photos by date, rename them with the date first, and move the blurry ones into a separate folder for you to review rather than deleting anything. Then I'll go through the unopened newsletters from this week and give you a line or two on each.
Action: Find the March break folder in Drive and start with the rename, keeping a list of old and new names so it can be undone, then summarize the roughly 12 unread newsletters.

That's lovely, I'm glad the flowers from the Mumbai florist landed and that the call with her went so well. I'll note Mom's birthday as Nov 3.
Action: Add Mom's birthday, Nov 3, as a yearly calendar entry with a reminder a week before, note the Mumbai florist as your usual, and hold the book order for Priya until you decide tonight.

Sending the Hannah text now. I don't have the final Instant Payouts v1 scope in front of me, so I'll pull what's actually in v1 from the project docs rather than guess at features, and keep the blurb to 4 or 5 lines for her sales deck.
Action: Send the text to Hannah, then read the v1 scope and draft the blurb for you to review before it goes to Olivia.

Here's a draft: 'Hi team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That's 10,000 times the product did its job, and it comes from the steady work each of you put in. Thank you.' It's warm and plain, with no hype.
Action: Tell me one or two people and what they did and I'll add a specific thank-you, then save it for you to post tomorrow.

Booking East End Plumbing for Monday morning, 29 Jun. For the Lattice self-review due Fri 10 Jul, I'll remind you to start on Tue 30 Jun, since Monday is the plumber, and again on Mon 6 Jul, the week it's due.
Action: Book East End for Mon 29 Jun morning at 41 Curzon St, then set the two reminders for the Lattice self-review.

Since you prefer Canadian retailers and skip Amazon when a local option ships within a week, I'll start with Indigo. I'll look for a B2-level Spanish grammar book with a strong subjunctive section, plenty of exercises and an answer key, and check that its examples aren't all Castilian, since you want Mexican vocabulary.
Action: Search Indigo for 2-3 candidates, check shipping time, and send you the shortlist with prices, then order your pick (falling back to another Canadian retailer only if Indigo can't ship within a week).

For quotes, I'd start about 4 to 6 weeks before the renewal date, which should be on the letter, so there's time to compare and line up the new policy before the old one lapses. Notice to cancel depends on your insurer and province, so I won't guess; the safe order is usually to get the new policy in place first, then cancel the old one in writing.
Action: Send the school council reply now, then find the renewal date in the letter or your email and set a reminder to start quotes 6 weeks ahead.

Holding the order. The basement kitchen has a microwave, an induction hotplate and the old fridge, and the hotplate needs flat-bottom induction pans: the cast iron works, the old aluminium pot doesn't. When you ask Sam, note that he gets migraines from strong fragrances, so the Febreze plug-in and Glade candles are out and the unscented charcoal bags are the safe option.
Action: Keep the order on hold, and for the week's cooking I can suggest simple one-pan meals that suit cast iron and the microwave, vegetarian for Sam with no fish, and nothing with cashews or pistachios for Leo.

I don't have Sam's usual coffee order or any food restrictions on hand, and I'd rather not guess for a long evening of interviews. Tell me what he likes and I'll set up a delivery to Riverdale, room 214, for around 3:30, after checking the school office accepts deliveries.
Action: Find cafes near Riverdale that can deliver by 3:30 while I wait for his order.

I'll read Sam's text first, since it may already settle dinner. For tonight with no hotplate, that means takeout or something microwave-friendly, and whatever we pick needs to be vegetarian with no fish or seafood for Sam, free of cashews and pistachios for Leo, and with no cilantro for you.
Action: Read Sam's message, then suggest 2-3 options that fit and place the order once you pick.

On it. I'll go through this week's inbox and sort it into needs a reply, just FYI, and safe to ignore, and I won't send anything.
Action: Scan this week's email and give you a short list with who wrote, what they want, and any deadline, with the ones that actually need you at the top.

Got it, March break week of the 16th, just you and Leo. Per your hotel rule I'll only consider fully refundable rates, ideally walkable to transit (I'll tell you if Drumheller doesn't really offer that). Leo was born July 17, 2019, so he'll be 6 then and I'll use that for the Tyrrell child ticket price, and because 3 nights will be over $100 I'll check with you before booking anything.
Action: Find fully refundable hotel options for 3 nights, check Tyrrell's price for a 6-year-old, and send both for your OK. Which 3 nights do you want?

I don't have your basement kitchen setup saved, and I'd rather not guess when you're planning a week of cooking. I'll check your notes for it first, and keep the order on hold.
Action: Search your notes for the basement kitchen, and if nothing turns up, ask you to list what's down there (appliances, sink, fridge) so I can suggest realistic meals.

I don't have a record of what you said helps you unwind on weekends, and I'd rather not make it up when you're fried. I can search your notes and past chats for it, and meanwhile keep tomorrow low-effort: a slow morning, one easy thing, and nothing else scheduled.
Action: Search your notes for what helps you unwind and come back with a simple plan for tomorrow.

I don't have your collection area or this year's yard waste schedule saved, so I can't give you an end date without guessing. Six bags is a fair amount, so it's worth getting the last pickup date right.
Action: Look up this year's yard waste schedule for your address on your city's collection calendar and tell you the last pickup date; if I can't find your address, I'll ask you for the postal code.

The one that probably matters is the Queen St E watermain work between Leslie and Jones from May 19, about 9 weeks of lane restrictions and 501 streetcar delays; if that's your streetcar to King St West on your Tuesday and Thursday office days, allow extra time. Otherwise, the Leslieville Flea is Sun May 24 at Ashbridge Estate, Hearth Bakehouse opens May 15, the movie night poll closes May 31, and the Green P lot at Coxwell & Queen closes June 1-14, next month.
Action: If your commute does use the 501, I'll put a heads-up on your calendar for May 19, and I can add the Flea on May 24 too.

On it. I'll go through this week's inbox and sort it into needs a reply, just FYI, and safe to ignore, skipping promos entirely (including from the senders you unsubscribed from in January). I won't send anything.
Action: Scan this week's email and give you a short list with who wrote, what they want, and any deadline.

Sorry about the dehumidifier. Your receipts get auto-labelled 'Receipts' now, but that filter is newer than a summer purchase, so I'll search your whole inbox as well as that label. Once I find the receipt I'll check the purchase date against the warranty terms.
Action: Search the Receipts label and your inbox for the dehumidifier receipt, then check the warranty on it and tell you whether you're still covered.

The thing I have noted is the Canadian Tulip Festival in Ottawa in May 2026, which you'd floated for Sam's parents, with a note to check dates in April; I haven't confirmed this year's dates against the long weekend yet. If Grace and Daniel are in Ottawa, you'd likely want to drive the Mazda and leave early Friday with the Big Apple stop in Colborne, which Leo treats as a rule.
Action: Check the festival dates for May 2026 against the long weekend and send you what's on, plus the drive plan.

Sorry about the heel. It may be worth mentioning the plantar fasciitis from earlier this year to the physio, even though Marcus's calf stretches helped then. I'll look for next week after 5:30 pm on a weekday, which you prefer for appointments like this, or Saturday after your 7:30 run with Marcus, and your Lumen Pay wellness account may cover part of it.
Action: Find physio openings next week (weekdays after 5:30 pm or Saturday late morning onward), book the earliest one that works, and tell you the time and cost.

Partly. Written Portuguese is quite readable if you know Spanish, so signs and menus will mostly make sense, but spoken Portuguese sounds very different and you'll often miss it. Many people in Lisbon will also switch to English, so I'd learn a handful of Portuguese phrases and not lean on Spanish alone.
Action: Put together a short Lisbon cheat sheet and a role-play or two (ordering food, asking directions), since role-play is how you learn best.

Booking Dr. Lin at Queen East Dental for Apr 22, late morning. Apr 22 is a Wednesday and your 1:1 with Tom Becker is 11:30-12:00, so I'd aim for a slot that ends well before 11:30, like 10:00 or 10:30; if nothing fits I'll offer the nearest other days.
Action: Request Dr. Lin at Queen East Dental (1046 Queen St E) for Apr 22 around 10:00-10:30 and confirm the time with you.

Here's a draft: 'Hey! Leo and I are heading to Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30 for the playground and the market. Want to come with the kids? No pressure if the week wiped you out.'
Action: Hold it for your OK, then send it to Hannah as is or with your edits.

Sending the reply to Jenna. For paint cans, a dead printer and batteries, those are three different drop-off types (paint is hazardous waste, the printer is e-waste, batteries often have retail drop boxes), so I'd rather check what's actually near you in Leslieville than guess.
Action: Send the street party reply, then look up the City of Toronto's drop-off options for paint, electronics and batteries closest to you and send addresses and hours.

I'll pull the grocery spending from your TD statements for October, August and September and compare the three months. I don't have the figures in front of me, so I won't estimate them.
Action: Open the TD statements for Aug, Sep and Oct, total the grocery transactions for each month, and send you the three numbers with the differences and which stores I counted.

I don't have where Sam's parents live or what time school pickup is, so I can't give you an honest arrival time yet. I'll check your contacts and calendar for both.
Action: Look up Sam's parents' address and Friday pickup time, then estimate the drive for a Friday departure right after pickup; if I can't find them, I'll ask you for the town and pickup time.

Booking East End Plumbing for Monday morning, 29 Jun. For the Lattice self-review due Fri 10 Jul, I'll remind you to start on Tue 30 Jun, since Monday is the plumber, and again on Mon 6 Jul, the week it's due.
Action: Book East End for Mon 29 Jun morning, then set the two reminders for the Lattice self-review.

Here's a checklist for DES-341, the two schedule picker copy variants: 1) does each say clearly what happens and when, 2) is the tone consistent with the rest of the product copy, 3) does it fit the UI without truncating, 4) are any timing or fee claims accurate, and 5) can you pick one and say why in a sentence. Once you pick, replying on DES-341 should unblock PAY-1182.
Action: Save the checklist to a note linked to DES-341 and nudge you after lunch.

Here's a draft: 'Neha, [partner's name], here's to a lifetime of one of you saying I'm fine with whatever, and the other knowing that's a trap. May you always agree on the thermostat, and when you don't, may the right one win gracefully. Congratulations, cheers.' I don't have the partner's name, so there's a placeholder.
Action: Fill in the name once you send it, and adjust the jokes if you want something more specific to the two of them.
